question: What happens if a human falls into a black hole?
short_answer: If a human falls into a stellar-mass black hole, extreme gravitational tidal forces stretch the body vertically and compress it horizontally—a process known as 'spaghettification'. Before reaching the singularity, the intense gradient breaks apart molecular and atomic bonds.
full_explanation: Stellar-mass black holes exert immense gravitational tidal forces over short distances. Because gravity falls off with the square of distance, your feet experience a significantly higher pull than your head, pulling your body into a thin string of matter before crossing the event horizon.
